name: Roski sculpture studio and shared woodshop
school: USC Roski School of Art and Design
blurb: The Watt Hall sculpture facility: a wood and metal shop with full-time technical support, a bronze-casting foundry, welding stations and a moldmaking area, plus a woodshop shared by enrolled Roski and Architecture students. The Galen Ceramics Studio with wheels and kilns is next door in Watt Hall 107.
hours_note: Tool crib: Monday to Thursday 9 AM to 9 PM, Friday 9 AM to 5 PM. The page says the studios are accessible 24 hours a day to its students.

access.note: The page says the woodshop is open to enrolled Roski and Architecture students. Ask Roski whether you can use it.

access_steps: Ask at the tool crib, which checks out hand and power tools.

equipment.name: Shared woodshop: table saw, radial arm saw, band saw, jig saw, panel saw, chop saw, planer, sander and grinder, lathe, shears and drill press
equipment.plain_name: Woodshop (saws, sanders and a drill press for cutting and shaping wood)

equipment.name: Wood and metal shop with welding stations (oxy-acetylene, arc and MIG) and plasma cutters
equipment.work_area_note: Plasma cutters cut mild steel up to 3/4 in

equipment.name: Tool crib: hand and power tools to check out
equipment.plain_name: Hand and power tools to borrow

services.name: Bronze casting foundry and moldmaking area (plaster, latex, slipcast and silicone molds)
Galen Ceramics Studio, Watt Hall 107: electric wheels, a slab roller, extruders, and electric, soda and gas kilns

first_visit: You will likely need your USC ID.
There is likely a short safety orientation before you first use the tools.
Ask staff which training your tool needs; it typically differs by tool.
estimates.training_note: Cutting, power and machine tools likely need an orientation plus training on that tool. Ask staff before you plan around one.
estimates.cost_note: You likely pay for materials only. Where this space lists no price, cost ranges use typical prices for buying the material yourself.
